Environment Domains Catalog

The platform architecture decouples environment domain specifications from image processing plumbing. River and Landslide are active in the MVP.

River Basin & Riparian Corridor

Primary MVP Environment

Monitors fluvial corridors, riverbanks, and active channels for morphology changes, erosion risks, sediment deposition, and water-surface extent shifts.

Supported Detection Findings (6)

Potential Riverbank Erosion
High

Detected lateral bank retreat or embankment collapse along the river boundary.

Recommended Protocol: Initiate field verification, evaluate embankment integrity, and alert local water authority.
Significant Water-Area Change
Medium

Substantial widening, narrowing, or migration of active surface water footprint.

Recommended Protocol: Cross-reference hydrological flow gauge data and inspect upstream discharge controls.
Exposed Riverbed
Medium

Significant de-watering revealing submerged gravel bars, sediment shelves, or channel bed.

Recommended Protocol: Assess ecological flow compliance and evaluate localized drought or diversion stress.
Potential Sediment-Related / Exposed-Bed Change
Low

Visible accumulation of high-reflectance silt or sand deposits indicating deposition or scour.

Recommended Protocol: Perform sediment budget review and verify navigation / intake channel clearance.
Riverbank Movement
Medium

Gradual meander shifting or channel realignment observed between comparative timestamps.

Recommended Protocol: Update cadastral boundary mapping and schedule seasonal channel morphology survey.
Other Significant Water-Body Change
Low

Unclassified surface water anomaly, backwater inundation, or oxbow lake disconnection.

Recommended Protocol: Conduct localized drone or ground reconnaissance.

Domain Investigation Questions (4)

River Name and Basin / ReachRequired input
Has there been a significant precipitation or dam discharge event within the last 14 days?Required input
Hydrological Stage ComparisonRequired input
Proximity to downstream bridges, flood embankments, or inhabited zonesOptional context

Slope & Landslide Risk Corridor

Secondary MVP Environment

Monitors mountainous and hilly terrain for slope failure, crown scarp development, abrupt vegetation canopy loss, and debris flow displacement.

Supported Detection Findings (4)

Potential Landslide-related Change
Critical

Composite detection of crown scarp, displaced slope material, or debris trail.

Recommended Protocol: Dispatch geological hazard assessment unit and verify downslope transit corridor safety.
Potential Terrain Disturbance
High

Disruption of slope surface texture, tensile cracks, or localized earth slip.

Recommended Protocol: Install slope extensometers or conduct UAV photogrammetry survey.
Vegetation Loss / Canopy Stripping
Medium

Rapid depletion of forest canopy exposing underlying soil or bedrock on inclined terrain.

Recommended Protocol: Cross-reference with forestry logging records and inspect for underlying slip vectors.
Exposed Ground & Colluvium
Medium

Spectral signature transition from vegetated cover to bare geological substrate or talus.

Recommended Protocol: Assess catchment erosion potential and sediment delivery to drainage channels.

Domain Investigation Questions (4)

Slope / Mountain Range SectorRequired input
Antecedent Precipitation Conditions (Past 72 hours)Required input
Estimated Slope GradientOptional context
Elements at Downslope RiskRequired input
